business_problem: Bell Canada's escalation managers were spending the opening minutes of high-stakes customer complaints on intake administration because case fields were incomplete, duplicates had to be found manually, and routing had to be confirmed before work could begin.
solution_summary: Bell Canada and Ateko focused automation on the intake layer of escalation management rather than on the sensitive customer conversation itself. Using AI Agents, Bell now creates complaint cases automatically, validates whether required information is complete, fills in critical fields, detects duplicate complaints across channels, and routes each case to the right escalation team before a manager engages. Telecommunications Service Management provides the governed service workflow context around those escalations, while Now Assist supports the broader AI-enabled service environment. The result is that human escalation managers receive cases that are already prepared, verified, and assigned, so they can spend their first minutes solving the customer's actual problem instead of performing administrative triage on an interaction where trust is already at risk.

data_flow: A complaint enters Bell's intake layer, where AI Agents create the case, verify completeness, populate fields, detect duplicates, and route it to the correct escalation team. The prepared record is then handled in Bell's telecommunications service workflow so a manager starts with a trusted, ready-to-work case instead of manual triage.
business_outcome: Bell reduced customer response time by 25% on escalation cases and achieved 90% accuracy on AI-assisted cases, allowing managers to start with complete, validated, and correctly routed complaints instead of spending time on intake cleanup.
